propositions: Three sources (lock module docstring, concurrency docs, integration tests) contradict each other on whether dual_window is transient migration scaffolding or permanent contract.

The lock module docstring falsely frames dual_window as a temporary migration window that flips to False after bash retirement, contradicting the surviving code's dependence on permanent dual-leg behavior.
The concurrency documentation describes the retired bash _flock_stage_commit as the active write path instead of the current Python fcntl+mkdir dual-window mechanism.
The dual-window lock (fcntl for speed + mkdir for portability on no-flock platforms) is the intended permanent write-lock contract and must be documented and tested as such.
No enforcing test currently verifies that the default lock behavior creates both fcntl and mkdir artifacts, nor that dual_window=False disables the mkdir leg.
